subject: ss-surgical-gastroenterology
title: Small bowel colorectal and anorectal surgery: obstruction Crohn ulcerative colitis diverticular disease and anal surgery

steps.tx: **Small bowel obstruction accounts for 20 percent** of emergency laparotomies with 60 percent from adhesions. Colicky pain with vomiting and absolute constipation is typical. Air fluid levels on erect X-ray appear in 70 percent of mechanical cases. Closed loop obstruction strangulates in 10 percent and needs emergency surgery.
steps.say: Start small bowel obstruction with the adhesion history that dominates emergency admissions. Colicky pain with repeated vomiting and complete stoppage of stool passage guides the diagnosis. Plain films show stacked air fluid levels, while a strangulated loop shows wall thickening and needs theatre without delay.

steps.tx: Crohn disease transmural inflammation **affects ileocaecal area in 70 percent** of cases. Skip lesions with cobblestone mucosa characterise 40 percent on endoscopy. Strictures under 2 cm cause obstructive symptoms in 30 percent. Smoking doubles recurrence risk after resection in cohort studies.
steps.say: Imagine Crohn disease as full thickness inflammation that can strike any gut segment in patches. The terminal ileum suffers most often, and tobacco use doubles the chance of relapse after surgery. Narrow strictures that block the lumen need strictureplasty or limited resection rather than wide bowel sacrifice.

steps.tx: **Ulcerative colitis begins in rectum in 90 percent** of cases and spreads proximally continuously. Bloody diarrhoea occurs in 95 percent during flares. Toxic megacolon with 9 cm diameter complicates 5 percent of attacks. Prophylactic colectomy reduces cancer risk from 15 percent to under 2 percent after 10 years of disease.
steps.say: See ulcerative colitis as continuous mucosal disease that never skips patches. Bloody diarrhoea with urgency dominates the history, and a massively dilated colon signals toxic dilatation. Long standing disease raises cancer risk enough that many patients choose colectomy after a decade of colitis.

steps.tx: **Diverticular disease affects 30 percent of adults** over 60 years with 5 percent developing diverticulitis. Pericolic abscess stage 1b appears in 20 percent of perforated cases. Hinchey stage 3 free perforation needs sigmoid resection in 15 percent. Recurrence after conservative care reaches 20 percent within 5 years.
steps.say: Examine diverticular disease for the left iliac fossa pain that brings older adults to the emergency unit. Most diverticula stay silent, but a small fraction inflame and perforate into abscess or free peritonitis. Hinchey staging decides between drainage, washout, and resection, with recurrence remaining common after antibiotics alone.

steps.tx: **Massive lower GI bleeding stops spontaneously in 80 percent** of diverticular bleeds. CTA detects active extravasation at 0.3 mL per minute flow. Angiographic embolisation succeeds in 70 percent without colectomy. Ischaemia follows embolisation in under 5 percent when superselective technique is used.
steps.say: Check massive lower bleeding for the diverticular source that stops by itself in most patients. CT angiography pinpoints the bleeding point when bleeding continues, and embolisation saves the colon in many. Wide colectomy stays as rescue for uncontrolled bleeding or ischaemia after embolisation.

steps.tx: **Ischaemic colitis follows SMA occlusion in 30 percent** of cases with pain out of proportion. Pneumatosis on CT appears in 15 percent and suggests transmural necrosis. Early laparotomy for peritonitis saves 40 percent versus delayed surgery. Segmental resection without primary anastomosis is safer in 20 percent with gross ischaemia.
steps.say: Compare ischaemic pain with the tenderness on examination, where severe pain with soft abdomen suggests early ischaemia. Gas in the wall on CT warns of dead bowel, and waiting for peritonitis loses bowel length. Early exploration with second look laparotomy limits resection to truly dead segments.

steps.tx: **Pilonidal disease presents at 15 years** in hairy young men with midline pits in 90 percent. Abscess needs emergency drainage through lateral incision. Elective excision with secondary healing recurs in 10 percent. Flap cover reduces recurrence to 5 percent in chronic disease.
steps.say: Discuss pilonidal sinuses as young adult disease of the natal cleft where hair drives infection. Acute abscess needs prompt drainage away from the midline, while chronic pits suit elective excision. Secondary healing invites hair again, so flap reconstruction keeps recurrence lower in repeatedly infected patients.

steps.tx: **Haemorrhoidal disease causes bleeding in 40 percent** of adults presenting to colorectal clinics. Grade 3 piles prolapse needing manual reduction in 30 percent. Stapled haemorrhoidopexy causes 2 cm anal stenosis in under 2 percent. Fistula recurrence reaches 5 percent after lay open surgery.
steps.say: Review haemorrhoids for the bright red bleeding that coats stool rather than mixing with it. Higher grades prolapse beyond the anal verge and need manual replacement. Stapling preserves the anal canal, while excision suits external piles with skin tags and thrombosis.

steps.tx: **Anal fissure in 20 percent is posterior midline** and bleeds on defaecation. Chronic fissure with sentinel tag persists beyond 8 weeks in 30 percent. Lateral internal sphincterotomy heals 90 percent of chronic cases. Topical nifedipine heals 50 percent of acute fissures without surgery.
steps.say: Distinguish fissure pain that lasts hours after stool passage from pile discomfort. Posterior tears dominate, and a sentinel tag marks chronicity beyond two months. Sphincterotomy divides the tight sphincter that perpetuates ischaemia, while topical therapy controls pain in early acute disease.

steps.tx: Complications include **anastomotic leak in 5 percent after colectomy** and pelvic abscess in 10 percent. Short bowel syndrome under 200 cm remnant causes diarrhoea in 15 percent. Pouchitis after ileal pouch surgery affects 30 percent within 2 years. Fistula recurrence after Crohn resection reaches 20 percent at 5 years.
steps.say: Consider the leak and abscess risks that follow colorectal anastomosis, especially with low rectal joins. Short residual bowel struggles with fluids and nutrition for months. Pouchitis later plagues ileal pouches with fever and discharge, while Crohn recurrence favours the anastomosis within years of resection.

steps.tx: **Adhesions cause 60 percent of small bowel obstruction** and need no surgery when settling within 3 days. Ileocaecal Crohn affects 70 percent and strictures under 2 cm need limited resection. Toxic megacolon 9 cm complicates ulcerative colitis in 5 percent. Sphincterotomy heals 90 percent of chronic fissures after 8 weeks persistence.
steps.say: High-yield for the exam, remember the adhesion proportion, the ileocaecal share, and the megacolon diameter. Chronic fissure timing of eight weeks separates topical from surgical care. Anastomotic leak near five percent stays the commonest reason for reoperation after colectomy in viva answers.
